parsed.result: One focused change this pass, in the hero's own files only. **Fixed (2 criticals + 1 warning): lead paragraph legibility at tablet and mobile** `src/app/sections/hero/hero-stage.client.tsx` - the lead block was pinned to the foot of the stage with `mt-auto mb-9` below `lg`. That parked it on the hull and the dark water at 768px and 390px, where the 48% quiet run measured ~1.3:1 and four of five lines were effectively invisible. It now follows the title in normal flow with `mt-16` (64px = `--space-3xl`), which is exactly what spec Section 1 / Responsive prescribes (`768-1023: align-self: center; margin-top: 64px`, `< 768: width: calc(100% - 48px)`) - the quiet sky band the 48% colour was drawn against. The `lg` branch (96px below the title, right gutter, 431px measure) is unchanged. The text token was not touched, as the reviewer asked. Follow-on: stage `min-height` 680px → the spec's 620px, since the extra height existed only to open water for the bottom-parked block. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint src/app/sections/hero --max-warnings=0` both clean. **Left alone, with reasons (recorded in the summary JSON):** - **Vessel plate too dark** - this is the asset, not the code: no `opacity` or `mix-blend-mode` is applied to the vessel `` anywhere (checked the component and all four `hero-*` utilities in `globals.css`). Spec Section 1 says node `247:655` composites two image fills and must be exported flattened; `hero-vessel.png` was resolved from a single `imageRef`, so it carries only the darker fill. The remedy is to re-render `247:655` through the Figma render endpoint and overwrite that PNG - binaries are off-limits and auto-reverted this turn, so it needs its own asset pass. - **Exposure / Matter** - no WOFF2 exists in the repo and the wiring is in `fonts.ts` / `layout.tsx` / `globals.css`, all shared files another agent owns this pass. - **148px / 96px margin-tops** - literal spec values on the 4px grid with named tokens; the audit's list just tops out at 64px, so snapping would be an 84px/32px fidelity regression.
